candidates.change_summary: Add msg.value plus one extra wei to the recorded balance instead of exactly msg.value.
Delete the balance update so sent value is never recorded.
Remove the lock acquisition so reentrant calls are no longer blocked, allowing reentrant addToBalance to update balances in sequences the original reverts on.
Remove the lock release so the contract permanently locks after the first guarded call, making all subsequent addToBalance calls revert instead of updating balances.
Return the caller's balance instead of the queried address's balance.
Return zero instead of the stored balance of u.
Return the balance plus one, shifting every reported value.
Remove the nonReentrant_ modifier from addToBalance so reentrancy protection is gone.
Replace the accumulating addition with a plain assignment of msg.value, discarding the prior balance.
Delete the trailing locked_ = false; so the lock never resets and later addToBalance calls revert.
Delete the statement that zeroes the caller's balance after withdrawal, so funds can be withdrawn repeatedly.
Replace zeroing the balance with incrementing it by 1, so after a withdrawal the recorded balance is one wei instead of zero.
Move the balance-zeroing statement before the external call, so a reentrant callee observes a zeroed balance during the call.
Remove the reentrancy lock check from the nonReentrant_ modifier, allowing reentrant calls that observe different balances during withdrawal.
Delete the statement resetting the caller's balance, allowing repeated withdrawals so userBalance is never zeroed.
Replace the balance reset with an increment of 1 so a leftover balance of 1 remains after withdrawal.
Delete setting locked_ to true, disabling the reentrancy guard so a reentrant withdrawBalance can send funds twice before the balance is reset.
Delete resetting locked_ to false after execution, so locked_ stays true forever and withdrawBalance (and addToBalance) revert, never zeroing the balance.
Invert the guard condition to require(locked_), making all guarded calls revert so the balance is never credited or cleared as in the original.
